My first reply had mistakes in it — parts written wrong, and a word that was no material at all. The bench would have thrown that out, so here it is again, set down clean.

What I mended from the refused drawing: the sieve arms and conrods hung in the air, so I parented them to the sieve box, which they pull and push — that is how a sieve is worked, arms fixed to the box. And I set two posts under the arms' far ends at the south side, so they rest on something. The crank shaft sits between the north rails and the north legs, so it cannot tip. The mesh and rim ride with the box, as they should. The box slides north and south a short way, the crank turns, and the arms and rods follow it, all touching something.

It stands at the mill, shakes the flour through the fine iron mesh, and the grit stays behind on top, which is what Gorm asked for.
